payload.text: Show the collaboration network among Columbia's 80 most prolific researchers in 2021-2024 with hierarchical edge bundling, grouping the researchers by field and subfield so that cross-field collaborations stand out.

payload.result:
Dataset: Columbia University publications, 2021-2024 (OpenAlex snapshot of 2026-11-23)
Works (papers, preprints, books, datasets, ...) published 2021-2024 with at least one author affiliated with Columbia University (OpenAlex institution I78577930 and its OpenAlex child institutions: NASA GISS, Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, ICAP, CZ Biohub NY), taken from the OpenAlex API on 2026-11-23 and never refreshed. Includes all co-authors and their institutions, the OpenAlex topic hierarchy, profiles of Columbia-affiliated authors, venues, outgoing references, yearly citation counts, keywords and funders.

Tables:
- authors (29,518 rows): Profiles of authors who are Columbia-affiliated on at least one snapshot work.
- authorship_institutions (619,528 rows): Institutions listed by each author on each work (an author can list se
... [1,841 characters truncated] ...
 had less time to be cited.
- citations lists every outgoing reference; only rows with cited_in_snapshot = true point to works that are themselves in this dataset (and therefore have metadata here).
- authors contains profiles only for authors who are Columbia-affiliated on at least one work in the snapshot; other co-authors appear only in authorships (name and id).
- Profile metrics in authors and sources (works_count, cited_by_count, h_index, ...) are global OpenAlex values for the whole career / whole venue, not restricted to this snapshot.
- Some works have no abstract (abstract is NULL), no topic, or no source.

Counting rules:
- authorships has one row per (work, author); count works with count(DISTINCT work_id) after joining it.
- authorships.is_columbia is true when that author lists a Columbia institution on that specific work.
- A work can have up to 3 topics in work_topics; works.primary_topic_* gives the single primary one.
- work_topics joins to topics for the full hierarchy domain > field > subfield > topic.

Relationships:
- works.work_id = authorships.work_id
- authorships.(work_id, author_order) = authorship_institutions.(work_id, author_order)
- authorship_institutions.institution_id = institutions.institution_id
- authorships.author_id = authors.author_id
- works.source_id = sources.source_id
- works.primary_topic_id = topics.topic_id
- work_topics.work_id = works.work_id ; work_topics.topic_id = topics.topic_id
- citations.citing_work_id = works.work_id
- citations.cited_work_id = works.work_id
- work_citations_by_year.work_id = works.work_id
- work_keywords.work_id = works.work_id
- work_funders.work_id = works.work_id

payload.decision: Rank known author IDs by distinct 2021–2024 snapshot works on which they list Columbia or an included child, descending then author ID ascending. Retain exactly 80; all snapshot work types count. Classify using those same affiliated works: modal field from primary work topics, then modal subfield within that field, excluding missing topics and breaking ties by classification ID. Links count distinct snapshot works on which both selected authors appear, irrespective of each author's affiliation on the shared work. Cross-field refers to different assigned author fields, not a work's interdisciplinarity.

args.acceptance_criteria: Show all 80 ranked researchers (including isolates) with a radial hierarchical edge bundle that visibly nests field and subfield. Orange cross-field links stand out from gray within-field links and link widths increase with shared works. Labels, field index with counts, and legend fit; show full names, group membership or shared-work counts on hover, allow selection/highlight and working controls for link category, minimum shared works and bundle strength. Default totals are 208 pairs, 94 cross-field, and 114 within-field.

Orange links stand out against gray, thicker links indicate more shared works, and the default counts match the data: 208 pairs, 94 cross-field and 114 within-field. The field index and legend fit, selection clearly highlights a researcher’s collaborations, and the hover, selection, highlight, and parameter checks all pass.

payload.text:
**94 of the 208 coauthor pairs (45.2%) connect researchers assigned to different fields.** The strongest cross-field pair is **Michal F. Lipson** (Engineering) and **Alexander L. Gaeta** (Physics and Astronomy), with **57 shared works**. [T2]

The interactive network shows all **80 researchers** across **14 fields and 35 subfields**, including **15** who did not coauthor with anyone else in the top 80. [T1] In the hierarchical edge bundle, numbered outer arcs mark fields and inner arcs mark subfields. Orange curves connect different fields; gray curves stay within a field. Thicker curves mean more shared works. Hover for details or click a researcher to keep their links highlighted. Use **Show links**, **Minimum shared works**, and **Bundle strength** to reduce clutter or isolate cross-field ties. [V1]

Researchers are ranked by distinct 2021–2024 OpenAlex works on which they listed Columbia or an included child institution. Each is assigned their most common field, then their most common subfield within that field, using the primary topics of those works. A link counts shared works in the snapshot, even if one of the two authors did not list Columbia on that work. So **cross-field** describes the two researchers’ assigned fields, not the subject of their shared work. The snapshot excludes works with more than 100 authors. [T1, T2]
